summary:
H.J. Res. 45 is a joint resolution of congressional disapproval under the Congressional Review Act, chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code. Its primary purpose is to nullify the Department of Education action relating to “Waivers and Modifications of Federal Student Loans,” including the Department’s website announcement titled “One-Time Federal Student Loan Debt Relief” and the Federal Register document titled “Federal Student Aid Programs (Federal Perkins Loan Program, Federal Family Education Loan Program, and William D. Ford Federal Direct Loan Program),” published at 87 Fed. Reg. 61512 on October 12, 2022.

The operative provision states that Congress disapproves the rule submitted by the Department of Education and that the rule “shall have no force or effect.” The resolution identifies the disapproved action as the material printed in the Congressional Record on March 22, 2023, at pages S903–S906, together with a March 17, 2023 Government Accountability Office letter of opinion concluding that the waivers and modifications constitute a “rule” under the Congressional Review Act.

The resolution does not amend any provision of the United States Code, establish a new program, confer new regulatory authority, impose reporting requirements, authorize appropriations, or appropriate funds. It contains no express exceptions, savings clauses, implementation deadlines, or delayed effective date. Its legal effect depends on enactment as a joint resolution under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, after which the identified Department of Education rule would be without force or effect pursuant to the resolution and the Congressional Review Act.
